title: Deidra:
length: about 80 s (about 70 s without the optional row)
headline: In prison she joined a WRAP class for the free pizza. Now she goes back to run that same group.
story: Deidra was in prison when she signed up for a WRAP class, because there was a pizza party. Today she is a CARES navigator at MHA, and she goes back to York to run the WRAP group she once sat in.
Her message is simple: don't give up. She is shy on camera, so the cut is short and lets her sentences breathe. It must feel light, warm and hopeful. The pizza line is allowed to make people smile.
do: Open on frame 1 with “I was in prison and I signed up…”. Hook text on frame 1.
Move the crop right. She sits right of center.
Caption WRAP in capitals. She says “rap”, the program is WRAP.
Let her short answers breathe. Cut only the long pauses.
Use the chalk B-roll only where it matches her words.
dont: Never use “Oh my gosh I'm so nervous” (02:58).
Nothing about her crime or sentence. She never says it. Do not add it.
Do not use the WRAP-for-workplaces question (03:03–03:48).
No prison footage and no stock images of a prison.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of 20260909_C4586.MP4 (Deidra, MHA office, Lincoln, 9 Sep 2026). Times are mm:ss in the source file. The transcript joins questions and answers in one line and labels most of them "Deidre". Questions are marked (Interviewer) here.
[00:00] (Interviewer) start. Introduce yourself.
[00:02] My name is Deidre. I am a CARES navigator for MHA and I've worked here about two years.
[00:11] (Interviewer) How did you first come across MHA?
[00:14] I was in prison and I signed up for the rap class because they were giving a pizza party.
[00:22] (Interviewer) What makes peer support different from traditional support?
[00:27] Peer support is different to me because people have those lived experiences and it's easier to talk to.
[00:33] (Interviewer) And then the next two questions are if you have any moments that you remember and what would you say to somebody who doesn't believe that they can recover? So I'll give you some time to think about those.
[00:52] (Interviewer) So is there any moments that you still think about or participant stories that have stuck with you or connections you've made? It could be general too like just maybe going in to York and being able like to connect with them. Not to give you your answer or anything.
[01:15] For me it would be going back to York and facilitating the rap group there because I was once on the other side of that group and just seeing a lot of the ladies that have been there or that are still there that I was there with. It's just I don't know I hope to be inspiring to them.
[01:33] (Interviewer) What would you say to someone who doesn't believe that they can recover?
[01:39] Just not to give up. It took me a long time to finally get to where that I am today and just to keep pushing. You'll have your good days and bad days. Don't give up.
[01:57] (Interviewer) What do you think people get wrong about our job?
[02:01] That we focus on mental health.
[02:03] (Interviewer) If someone watching has never heard of MHA what should they know?
[02:11] That we truly do care. We are here to support anyone. I don't know.
[02:21] (Interviewer) That was good. That was actually good. That like we really it's not just a job to us.
[02:29] Yeah it's not just a job we don't judge. We've all been there.
[02:33] (Interviewer) How has rap impacted your life?
[02:38] So before I did like NA and all those things that they tell you to do and then once I did rap it was like it's the way to like look at myself and like what I look like when I'm like on a good day and a bad day.
[02:58] (Nervous aside, never use.)
[03:03] (Interviewer) Do you think us having rap facilitators has benefited our organization? (The question is asked several ways until 03:45.)
[03:45] I think it helps everyone all around.
[03:50] (Interviewer) Anything else you would like to add or share about MHA and your work?
[04:00] I love what I do. Every day I feel like it's my way of giving back and I can relate with everyone that I work with in one way or another.
[04:12] (Crew thanks her, 04:12–04:20.)
